## Conference overview

*Preview by Adam Burke, p. 49. Reproduced in full.*


> The American Conference seems pretty wide-open for the 2026 season and it’s fair to wonder if any team will have the record or resume to represent the Group of Six in the College Football Playoff.

> There are four new head coaches and five second-year head coaches in the conference, so nine of the league’s 14 teams are tough to project.

> Tenured coaches might have an inside track this season, but anything could happen.

> In terms of preseason conference winner odds, only the MAC has a higher-priced favorite than the American and seven of the 14 teams are priced at +800 or lower.

> Navy is the tepid favorite here with one of the more tenured coaches in the conference, as Brian Newberry begins his fourth season at the helm.

> UTSA’s Jeff Traylor and Army’s Jeff Monken are the only two sideline bosses with more years under their belts than Newberry.

> It probably isn’t a coincidence that UTSA (+480) and Army (6-1) are the second and third favorites, respectively, behind Navy (+310).

> Life is tough in the American Conference for college football these days.

> As mentioned, nine of the 14 teams have head coaches hired within the last two seasons because this conference is a springboard to Power Four jobs.

> Furthermore, any players that stand out are going to be on the minds of SEC, ACC, Big Ten, and Big 12 teams that are looking to fill some voids and plug some holes.

> In some respects, the service academies have an advantage in that they aren’t watching players go out the door for NIL paydays, but they also can’t leverage the transfer portal to their advantage.

> Outside of Army and Navy, just about every program in the conference has fewer than 10 returning starters.

> But, that doesn’t mean they are immune to big personnel losses, especially in Navy’s case with QB Blake Horvath.

> In a high-variance conference, there should be money to be made, whether you can isolate overachievers or underachievers with props and futures before the season or on a weekly basis. american

## Quarterback themes


**From the conference preview (p. 49):**

> But, that doesn’t mean they are immune to big personnel losses, especially in Navy’s case with QB Blake Horvath.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 49*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 12 of 14 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Army Black Knights** (p. 50) — Rival Navy had the upper hand on Army heading into last season because QB Blake Horvath still had eligibility left, whereas Bryson Daily had exhausted his.

- **Charlotte 49ers** (p. 52) — Depth is still an issue here and probably the best QB on the roster (Harrell) will be out until mid-October or so.

- **Florida Atlantic Owls** (p. 57) — Veltkamp is really the only starting QB for FAU and he needs to be better.

- **Navy Midshipmen** (p. 61) — Every few years, it seems like a stud QB comes around in Annapolis and Horvath will be held in that light.

- **North Texas Eagles** (p. 63) — Tayven Jackson originally went to Tennessee and got some starts for Indiana and also UCF, so he’s the clubhouse leader to be the QB.

- **Rice Owls** (p. 65) — At Davidson back in 2024, Wildcats QBs only had 152 pass attempts in 11 games, as the team ran the ball 640 times for 3,720 yards, with QB Andrew Frazier third in rush attempts and rush yards.

- **South Florida Bulls** (p. 67) — At USF, most of those players are quarterbacks, as Hartline and OC Tim Beck got Michael Van Buren by way of Mississippi State and LSU and Luke Kromenhoek by way of Florida State and Mississippi State.

- **Temple Owls** (p. 69) — With Simon and backup Gevani McCoy gone, there is virtually no experience on the roster, with Penn State’s Jaxon Smolik, who played in four games over three years at Penn State, and Ajani Sheppard, who played five games at Rutgers and zero last season at Washington State, as the primary QB options.


*4 further teams also address this theme; see their team pages.*


## Returning-production themes


**From the conference preview (p. 49):**

> Outside of Army and Navy, just about every program in the conference has fewer than 10 returning starters.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 49*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 14 of 14 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Army Black Knights** (p. 50) — A Hellums injury would be brutal for Army, as they have no game experience behind him.

- **Charlotte 49ers** (p. 53) — This season, the starting gig may fall on the shoulders of Western Carolina transfer Cole Gonzales, at least until Harrell returns.

- **East Carolina Pirates** (p. 54) — If he has similar success this season, it will be a thoroughly impressive coaching job with virtually none of last season’s major contributors back in the fold.

- **Florida Atlantic Owls** (p. 56) — In a conference desperately lacking returning starters, Kittley has a couple handfuls of them and brought in 30 more players via the portal, including some defenders capable of creating negative plays.

- **Memphis Tigers** (p. 58) — It may take a year with new schemes and a ton of transfers, but Huff seems to be an outstanding coach based on the returns we’ve seen thus far.

- **Navy Midshipmen** (p. 61) — Tecza and Heidenreich, who was drafted in the seventh round by the Steelers, are monumental losses of production as well.

- **North Texas Eagles** (p. 62) — The top returning running back had 95 yards on 21 carries.

- **Rice Owls** (p. 65) — At Davidson back in 2024, Wildcats QBs only had 152 pass attempts in 11 games, as the team ran the ball 640 times for 3,720 yards, with QB Andrew Frazier third in rush attempts and rush yards.

## Transfer-portal themes


**From the conference preview (p. 49):**

> In some respects, the service academies have an advantage in that they aren’t watching players go out the door for NIL paydays, but they also can’t leverage the transfer portal to their advantage.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 49*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 11 of 14 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Charlotte 49ers** (p. 53) — Neither the incoming class nor the portal class graded all that highly for 247Sports relative to the rest of the conference, but there are a lot more warm bodies and some of them are probably better at football than the ones that were there.

- **East Carolina Pirates** (p. 55) — Davis got backup RB Ashton Gray to transfer and also WR Landon Sides, so he has skill guys who know the scheme.

- **Florida Atlantic Owls** (p. 56) — In a conference desperately lacking returning starters, Kittley has a couple handfuls of them and brought in 30 more players via the portal, including some defenders capable of creating negative plays.

- **Memphis Tigers** (p. 58) — This is a great spot for Huff, who has a lot of NIL money to play with and a pretty solid program that hasn’t had a losing season since 2013.

- **North Texas Eagles** (p. 62) — Things like this are possible in the transfer portal era, but this may very well be the most stripped-down program we’ve ever seen.

- **Rice Owls** (p. 64) — It’s a tough gig and it looks like another tough year, but Abell seems up for the challenge and brought in a decent number of P4 transfers.

- **South Florida Bulls** (p. 67) — The transfer portal gives players with that kind of pedigree the chance to go to a G6 program and attempt to get back on the radar.

- **Tulane Green Wave** (p. 71) — The fact that Retzlaff was available was truly a gift for Tulane because they were not set up well at the running back position with Makhi Hughes’ transfer.


*3 further teams also address this theme; see their team pages.*


## Schedule themes


**From the conference preview (p. 49):**

> *Not addressed in guide.*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 12 of 14 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Army Black Knights** (p. 50) — The Black Knights play at a rest disadvantage in each of their first three October games and UTSA is the only team projected in the top-half of the conference that they avoid.

- **Charlotte 49ers** (p. 52) — The product on the field should look better, but finding two more wins on the schedule than last season is a chore.

- **East Carolina Pirates** (p. 54) — Harrell also owns upset wins over two ACC programs in bowl games, including in-state rival NC State, who did get revenge in the season opener last year, but in a very competitive 24-17 game.

- **Florida Atlantic Owls** (p. 56) — The back half of the schedule is a bit of a challenge, but this was a 4-8 team with a -21 TO margin that definitely has more talent in Year 2 of this new system.

- **Memphis Tigers** (p. 58) — Memphis went from Group of Five College Football Playoff contender to an afterthought in a hurry, as the Tigers lost to Tulane at home and then followed that up with three straight losses, including a defeat in the Gasparilla Bowl after head coach Ryan Silverfield left for Arkansas and a ton of players left the program.

- **Navy Midshipmen** (p. 60) — The conference schedule is not too demanding for Navy and they should be better than both service academies again.

- **North Texas Eagles** (p. 62) — They’ll go to Navy, UTSA, and Tulane, so the road games are very difficult.

- **Rice Owls** (p. 64) — Rice got a pretty favorable schedule last season, but that is not the case this season.

## Competing viewpoints and internal disagreements


### Coach tenure stated differently in different places


- **Brian Newberry (Navy Midshipmen)** — the preview (p. 49) describes his **4th** season; his team page (p. 60) states his **5th**. Preview wording: *"…Newberry begins his fourth season…"* Both are reproduced as printed; neither is corrected.

### Staff do not agree on a champion

5 teams received votes. UTSA leads with 10 of 22, but 12 votes went elsewhere (Navy 8, Memphis 2, East Carolina 1, South Florida 1). Recorded in full rather than reduced to a consensus.
